narrative:
The model estimated an 81% probability that you would be a bad credit risk, so your application was denied. That is a high-risk assessment, not a certainty, but it means the model found your application much closer to borrowers who struggled than to those who repaid.

The strongest factor was your checking account status: your account is below zero, a situation seen for only about 12.6% of approved applicants, while most approved applicants had no negative balance. This weighed heavily toward denial. The second factor was your credit history: having no credits or all paid is very uncommon among approved applicants and suggests a thin or less proven borrowing record, increasing the risk estimate. The third factor was the loan purpose: a new car was somewhat less common among approved applicants than radio/TV or furniture purchases, so it added to the risk, though less than the first two.

To improve your chances, avoid negative checking balances and build a documented repayment record, such as a small loan or credit-building product paid on time. Ask the lender what information could strengthen a future application, consider a smaller request, and see whether adding a creditworthy co-applicant or guarantor is possible. Reapply only when your account balance and credit history are stronger.
